correctness.rationale: The exact monomial beta-moment formula and s=t/(1-t) substitution give L_n(c)=e^{ic}Gamma(n+alpha+2)U(n+1,-alpha,-ic)/Gamma(alpha+1). At fixed alpha>-1,c>0 the established DLMF 13.8.11 and K-Bessel asymptotic yield a nonzero complex amplitude with relative O(n^-1/2) and phase sqrt(2c(n+1))+c/2-pi(alpha/2+1/4)/2. The real part has an absolute normalized error O(n^-1/2). The square-root phases are equidistributed by explicit O(sqrt N) exponential sum bounds; two-sided n cutoffs at log(1/t)^2/(2c) yield half-density and hence each signed coefficient 1/(4c). Polynomial times exp(-sqrt(2c n)) implies Schatten S_p for every p>0. All normalizations and fixed-parameter scope are stated. Separate exact finite moment checks and numerical asymptotic checks passed 98 assertions; finite tests are not treated as proof.

originality.rationale: The substantive claimed invariant is the exact common signed logarithmic-square counting coefficient 1/(4c), including independence of alpha and theta for a boundary-amplitude-one oscillatory symbol. The standard monomial diagonalization, Tricomi identity, Bessel asymptotic and phase equidistribution are acknowledged tools, not individually claimed as new. Compared scientific statements and implications in arXiv:2608.23733 (qualitative compactness), arXiv:2603.10879 (logarithmic-scale persistent oscillations), arXiv:1012.3528 (compact-support disk lower bounds and Bargmann cancellation), arXiv:1912.05855 (distributional-symbol trace class), and DLMF 13.8.11 (generic large-parameter asymptotics). None of their inspected results states or logically contains the signed counting law without nontrivial new object-specific reductions and phase counting. Best-knowledge status only.
residual_risks: A prior theorem on high-frequency radial Mellin transforms, perhaps phrased through generalized exponential integrals, might imply the same signed law without a Toeplitz label.
A general published theorem on singular-value asymptotics for oscillatory Toeplitz symbols may subsume the numerical constants despite negative targeted searches.
The special-function expansion is classical and not novel; originality attaches only to the exact signed spectral-counting implication for the specified operator family.

value.rationale: This is an exact natural signed spectral invariant for a bounded, smooth-in-disk, full-amplitude radial boundary oscillation. Its Toeplitz compression is in all Schatten classes, yet has infinitely many eigenvalues on both sides of zero, each obeying an explicit universal logarithmic-square Weyl coefficient independent of standard Bergman weight and phase. It distinguishes rapid reciprocal-distance oscillation from known slowly oscillating noncompact examples and quantifies cancellation not captured by qualitative Berezin compactness theorems. The special-function component is acknowledged as known; the motivated mathematical target is the all-weight/phase signed spectral distribution.
